status: REGISTERED. Approved by the author on 2026-10-24 (chat). Pushed in a commit of its own, before any O1 data were downloaded.
designed_after: Exploratory Pilot 2b on the 56 releases of January 2025 to October 2026 (thesis Chapter 5, Exploration after the tests): placebos passed; a median 94% of the long-run response within ten seconds; A_120 negative in 26 of 30 symbols, interval below zero in 2.
pipeline: thesis/evidence/o1_release_overshoot.py (download and per-symbol estimator from thesis/evidence/pilot2b_announcements.py, unchanged)
question: After scheduled US macro releases, does the response of small perpetuals to bitcoin's release-second move overshoot its long-run level, pooled across symbols with the shared releases respected?
releases: Every CPI and Employment Situation release (8:30 a.m. ET) and every FOMC statement (2:00 p.m. ET) in 2022-2024: 36 + 36 + 24 = 96 events on 95 dates (2024-06-12 carries CPI and FOMC). Sources: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2022/home.htm, https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2023/home.htm, https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2024/home.htm, https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (no unscheduled meetings or notation votes in these years).
symbols: The 30 USD-M perpetuals of Pilot 2b; evaluable with at least 40 usable releases; void if fewer than 15 evaluable.
freshness: The pilot used only 2025-2026 releases. Several 2022-2024 release dates appear in earlier data manifests of this project for other questions (bitcoin and major coins, one-minute data); no one-second release-window response of these 30 perpetuals has been computed.
estimator: Per symbol, the pilot's local projections: shock = bitcoin spot log price change from 1 s before to 10 s after the release; response b_j for j = 0..900 s with later bitcoin moves controlled; beta = mean b_j over 600-900 s; G_j = 1 - b_j/beta; A_H = sum of G_j over j = 10..9+H (seconds). Pooled Abar_H = mean over evaluable symbols.
bootstrap: Joint event bootstrap: 2,000 draws, seed 20261102; each draw resamples the release list with replacement and applies the same weights to every symbol.
validity: V1: pooled pre-release drift (mean over symbols of the slope of p^A(tau-1)-p^A(tau-301) on the shock, divided by beta) has a 95% joint-bootstrap interval covering zero
V2: median over symbols of sd(bitcoin 11-second move at pseudo-events 20 minutes before) / sd(at releases) below 0.5
The test is void if either fails.
primary: Overshoot: one-sided upper 95% joint-bootstrap bound of Abar_120 below zero (p < 0.05).
secondary: symbols with A_120 < 0, and with per-symbol interval below zero
median share through at 10 s; median beta
what_is_not_shown: Last-trade prices right after a release can be pushed by aggressive orders at the ask or bid; a pass shows a pooled transient response above the long-run level, not its mechanism.
prior_information: Pilot 2b point estimates (2025-2026 releases): pooled Abar_120 = -20.9 s; per-symbol A_120 negative in 26 of 30 but interval below zero in only 2. The pilot did not compute a joint-bootstrap interval, so how often the pooled prediction would pass on new releases is unknown.
opening_rule: The pipeline refuses to run unless the committed specification matches its hash and the counter is 0; it sets the counter to 1, downloads and evaluates once. Results, numbers, counter and download log are committed together.
